docs.title: Scenario reference
docs.text:
A scenario is one JSON (or YAML) object that holds every parameter of an experiment. It is validated against schemas/scenario.schema.json; the defaults below are the schema's. NNPM stores each saved scenario as a new version under scenarios/<name>/v<N>.json with its content hash (identical content reuses the version), and every run records the version it used, so a run can be replayed with run_experiment.sh --name <name> --version <N>.

Only name and model are required. Example files are in ../examples/scenarios/.

docs.title: Top level
docs.text: Field Type, default Meaning name string scenario name ([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*) description string free text pipeline experiment (default) or benchmarking the seven-stage pipeline, or the four-stage benchmarking pipeline of Appendix B (no load, no shaping) runtime string, testbed a registered runtime: testbed (per-layer profiling and partitioned inference), headsplit (the external HeadSplit runtime, see headsplit_integration.md) or a plug-in (see adding_a_runtime.md); the runtime's settings go in the block of the same name model string a registered model name: alexnet, vgg16, resnet50, gru_qoe, mobilenetv2, efficientnetb0, densenet121, keras_app, gpt2, tinyllama, llama32_1b, qwen25_05b, hf_decoder, fake, or a plug-in (see adding_a_model.md) model_args object the model's parameters (for example num_classes, seq_len, application, checkpoint), validated against the adapter's parameter schema and passed to every device tool devices list of node ids, or null (default) the end devices that take part; null means every End Device in nodes.json repetitions integer, 1 measured profiling repetitions per device warmup integer, 1 warm-up passes before the measured repetitions seed integer, 0 the random seed set on every device (random, NumPy, TensorFlow, PyTorch) settle_s number, 5 seconds between applying load and shaping and the start of profiling start_lead_s number, 3 how far in the future the start instant T0 is placed input object what the devices feed to the model: source (synthetic, default; numpy_file; image_file; image_folder; text_prompt), path (on the device, relative to its data directory), index (image_folder: which image of the sorted listing; class sub-directories give a label), text and tokenizer (text_prompt) checks object partition_equivalence (false): after profiling, every device compares each partition point with the unpartitioned model (python -m src.models.inference verify) and a relative deviation above tolerance (0.0001) aborts the run; the reports are collected under verification/ sweep object path (dotted field, for example network.default.added_rtt_ms) and values; expands into one run per value, each carrying sweep_origin (name, path, value) so that NNPM groups them

docs.title: edge_server
docs.text: Field Default Meaning policy SJF scheduling policy of the inference service: RR (one stage per request per round) or SJF (ascending offloaded work, ties by device index) nominal_frequency true pin the edge server's cores to their base frequency with turbo off for the run, restored at teardown profile_capacity true measure the edge server's FLOP/s on the model, used as C^R by the delay model port 5300 port of the inference service

docs.title: inference
docs.text: Field Default Meaning enabled false run partitioned inference against the edge-server service after profiling partition_points list the values of s to run (0 sends the raw input, S runs everything locally) repetitions 1 inferences per partition point

docs.title: network
docs.text:
A mapping from node id to a shaping block; the key default applies to every selected device. Shaping is applied with tc-netem on the device's data-plane interface (network_interface) at launch and removed at teardown.

Field Meaning delay_ms added egress delay in milliseconds added_rtt_ms extra round-trip time to the edge server, applied as egress delay; the Chapter 6 sweep variable from_map true derives delay_ms from the marker positions on the map (5 ms + 1 ms/km, clipped to [5, 50] ms) variation mode (constant; uniform: a new delay drawn from [min_ms, max_ms] every period_s; square: alternation between the delay and none every period_s) jitter_ms uniformly distributed random component of the delay loss_percent packet drop probability rate_mbps egress bandwidth cap (token-bucket filter) destinations node ids to shape separately (one netem leaf per destination); empty means all traffic of the interface background_traffic_mbps an iperf3 UDP stream from the device to the edge server at this rate for the whole run

docs.title: load
docs.text:
A mapping from node id to a load block (default applies to every selected device). The load generator runs on the device for the whole run; leave the node out of load for no injected load.

Field Default Meaning mode fixed fixed (one CPU and memory target); continuous (a new target drawn every cycle_s within cpu_range and memory_range); regime (the Chapter 3 regimes: light 10-20 % CPU and 10-20 % memory, moderate 30-50 % and 30-40 %, heavy 60-80 % and 50-60 %); processes (processes fully busy processes, the Chapter 4 background-process model) cpu_percent, memory_percent targets, in percent of one core (per worker) and of the device's memory cpu_range, memory_range [min, max] for the continuous mode regime light, moderate or heavy processes number of fully busy processes cores 1 number of CPU workers cycle_s 10 resampling cycle of the continuous modes period_ms 100 duty-cycle period of a CPU worker

docs.title: heterogeneity
docs.text:
A mapping from node id to a block (default applies to every selected device).

Field Meaning max_freq_mhz cap the CPU frequency with cpufreq (for example 1200 or 600 on a Raspberry Pi 4 at 1800) memory_limit_mb run the experiment processes in a cgroups v2 group with this memory limit threads number of threads the inference runtime may use

Every setting records the previous state and is restored at teardown.

docs.title: monitoring
docs.text: Field Default Meaning enabled true run the resource-monitoring agent on every device interval_s 1.0 sampling interval (CPU, memory, temperature, per-core frequency, throttling flags) power false run the INA260 power monitor power_interval_s 0.5 its sampling interval latency_pings 10 pings per target in the latency capture of the collect stage throughput false measure iperf3 throughput to the edge server throughput_duration_s 5 duration of that measurement

docs.title: optimisation
docs.text: Field Default Meaning enabled true run the partition optimiser after aggregation algorithm greedy a registered algorithm: greedy, exhaustive, trend_based, or a plug-in objective total_delay total_delay (sum of the per-device delays) or variance (population variance of the per-device delays) initial_scheme null starting vector: a JSON list, a {node: s} mapping or a percentage of the model depth ("50%") max_total_delays_ms null per-device limit on the total delay, a list or a {node: ms} mapping transmission_mode rtt_only rtt_only (the ping round-trip time) or size_over_rate (cut size over the measured rate plus the one-way latency) num_solutions, max_time_s 5, 300 parameters of the trend-based search

docs.title: headsplit
docs.text: Used when runtime is headsplit; the Create scenario dialog renders it from the runtime's schema. controller and workers (required) name nodes of nodes.json; model (the Hugging Face model name, TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 by default), tokens (50), prompt_length (256), mode (headsplit, head_only, layer_based, all), profile (path of the speculation-accuracy profile, relative to the HeadSplit directory), prompt, worker_memory_bytes, epsilon, alpha_min, memory_replace_threshold, rtt_margin, timeout_s, extra_args. See headsplit_integration.md. A plug-in runtime contributes its own block under its name.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
examples/scenarios/baseline.yaml: per-layer profiling of AlexNet on every device with no injected load (the benchmarking pipeline).

name: baseline
pipeline: benchmarking
model: alexnet
devices: null
repetitions: 3
warmup: 1
seed: 42
edge_server: {policy: SJF, nominal_frequency: true, profile_capacity: true}
monitoring: {enabled: true, interval_s: 1.0, latency_pings: 10}
optimisation: {enabled: true, algorithm: greedy, objective: total_delay, initial_scheme: "50%"}

examples/scenarios/local_demo.yaml: the fake model on two simulated devices with shaping, load and heterogeneity, runnable on any machine:

python -m src.orchestration.experiment run --scenario examples/scenarios/local_demo.yaml --local

The other examples: heavy_load.yaml (the heavy regime on every device), ch4_validation.yaml (the Chapter 4 procedure: AlexNet, four devices, partitioned inference at the table's partition points, RR and SJF), ch6_rtt_sweep.yaml (HeadSplit under a sweep of added round-trip times) and ch6_heterogeneity.yaml (HeadSplit with frequency caps and memory limits on the workers).

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
The testbed is designed for an isolated laboratory network: the access point and the management network hand out no default route and no upstream resolver, the devices are reachable only from the edge server, and the NNPM web application is served on the management network. The software is not hardened for exposure to the public internet; do not expose NNPM or the devices to untrusted networks.

Points that deserve attention when deploying:

  • SSH credentials. The edge server authenticates to the devices with a key (ssh_public_key_path) or a password taken from an environment variable; neither is stored in the repository or in config.yaml.
  • Privileges on the devices. Only tc and the heterogeneity module run with sudo -n, through a sudoers rule that names exactly those commands. Nothing else needs root.
  • NNPM access. Set nnpm_basic_auth_env in config.yaml to require HTTP basic authentication. Flask's debug mode is off by default and must never be enabled on the laboratory network.
  • Package integrity. Every Python dependency is installed with --require-hashes from the lock files, and the local mirror has a manifest with the SHA-256 of every file (python -m src.provisioning.mirror verify).

docs.title: Supported versions
docs.text: Security fixes are made on the main branch and included in the next release. The latest release is the supported one.

docs.title: Reporting a vulnerability
docs.text: Please do not open a public issue for a vulnerability. Report it privately through GitHub's "Report a vulnerability" form on the Security tab of the repository, or by e-mail to the maintainer listed in CITATION.cff and pyproject.toml. Include the affected component, the steps to reproduce and, if possible, a suggested fix. You will receive an acknowledgement within a week, and a fix or a mitigation will be published as soon as it is available.

docs.title: Setup guide
docs.text: How to assemble the testbed described in Chapter 3 of the thesis and bring it to the point where NNPM can run an experiment: hardware, networks, operating systems, time synchronisation, the package mirror and provisioning. The software installation itself is in installation.md; the step-by-step provisioning commands are in ../scripts/provision/README.md.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text:
Node Hardware Edge devices (five) Raspberry Pi 4 Model B: Broadcom BCM2711, four Cortex-A72 cores at 1.8 GHz, LPDDR4-3200 memory (two boards with 8 GB, three with 4 GB), 32 GB microSD card, on-board Cypress CYW43455 wireless chipset (one antenna chain, IEEE 802.11ac, 433 Mbit/s physical rate), Gigabit Ethernet. No accelerator. Edge server (one) Intel Core i7-5820K (6 cores, 3.3 GHz base, 3.6 GHz turbo), 32 GB DDR4, 512 GB NVMe SSD, Gigabit Ethernet, a USB IEEE 802.11ac adapter that hosts the access point. No accelerator. Power sensors (optional) one INA260 current-and-power sensor per device on the I2C bus. Network a small Ethernet switch for the management network; Ethernet cables.

Two devices (device1, device2 in nodes.example.json) have 8 GB and three have 4 GB, as in the thesis topology figure; in the Chapter 6 experiments the 8 GB board is the HeadSplit controller and four 4 GB boards are the workers. The run metadata records each node's real CPU model, core count, maximum frequency and memory on every run, so these facts are checked automatically.

Storage: the microSD card is the default; its read throughput (about 80 to 100 MB/s) can bottleneck model loading, which is why profiling records the model-load time separately from the inference time. A USB 3.0 SSD is an optional replacement.

docs.title: Bill of materials (indicative)
docs.text:
Prices are indicative, from 2024 to 2026 price lists, and vary by country and supplier.

Item Quantity Indicative unit price Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, 8 GB 2 85 EUR Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, 4 GB 3 60 EUR 32 GB microSD card (A1 class) 5 8 EUR USB-C power supply, 5 V 3 A 5 10 EUR Open rack or stackable cases, heat sinks 1 set 25 EUR Ethernet switch, 8 ports, unmanaged 1 20 EUR Ethernet cables 6 3 EUR USB IEEE 802.11ac adapter for the access point (a chipset with access-point mode support in Linux) 1 30 EUR INA260 breakout board (optional) 5 12 EUR

The five boards with cards and power supplies come to roughly 450 to 500 EUR; the rack, the switch, the cables and the WiFi adapter add about 100 EUR, the power sensors another 60 EUR. The statement in the thesis that an identical set-up can be assembled for under 500 EUR refers to the edge devices and their accessories; the edge server is not included.

docs.title: Physical layout
docs.text:
The devices sit on an open rack 2 to 3 m from the edge server, in line of sight of the access-point antenna. Each device has two network connections:

  • the data plane: the on-board WiFi joined to the edge server's access point; this is where inference traffic flows, where latency is measured and where tc-netem shaping is applied (network_interface, wlan0);
  • the management network: an Ethernet cable to the switch, which is connected to the edge server's wired interface; SSH, result collection, NTP and the package mirror use it (management_interface, eth0), so management traffic does not cross the wireless data plane during experiments.

nodes.json holds both addresses of every node (ip on the data plane, management_ip on the management network); config.yaml holds the two prefixes (base_ip_prefix, management_ip_prefix) and interface names. A single-network set-up (no switch) is possible: leave management_ip_prefix as null and omit management_ip; every subsystem then uses the wireless address.

docs.title: Addressing
docs.text: The example files use 192.168.0.0/24 for the data plane (edge server .1, devices .11 to .15) and 10.0.0.0/24 for the management network (same last octets). The edge server's dnsmasq serves both networks: a pool (.100 to .199) for devices that are not provisioned yet and for a laptop plugged into the switch, and a reservation per device name on the management network, so a freshly flashed device is reachable under its nodes.json address before it is provisioned. Provisioning then installs static addresses on both interfaces. Neither network hands out a default route or an upstream resolver: both are isolated, which keeps the measured delays free of foreign traffic.

docs.title: Operating systems
docs.text:
• Devices: Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit (Bookworm), which ships Python 3.11. The 64-bit variant is required: the LLM experiments exceed the 3 GB per-process limit of 32-bit address spaces, and provision_device.sh refuses a device whose kernel is not aarch64 (prepare_image.sh refuses a 32-bit image). Bookworm is the release named in the thesis software table (Appendix B, Table B.1); it ships Python 3.11.
  • Edge server: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Python 3.11 (python3.11, python3.11-venv) and NetworkManager (the Desktop default; on Ubuntu Server the management address is configured with netplan instead of the rendered NetworkManager profile).

docs.title: Access point
docs.text: provision_edge_server.sh renders /etc/hostapd/hostapd.conf from config.yaml: 5 GHz band (hw_mode=a), IEEE 802.11n/ac with an 80 MHz channel whose centre is derived from ap_channel, WPA2-PSK with the passphrase taken from the environment variable named by ap_passphrase_env (never written to config.yaml), the regulatory domain from ap_country. NetworkManager is told to leave the adapter alone and a small systemd unit gives it the edge server's data-plane address before hostapd starts. The achievable application-layer throughput per device is measured with src/network/throughput_measurement.py (the thesis quotes 80 to 120 Mbit/s for a single device; record the figure on your hardware, see the checklist).

docs.title: Time synchronisation
docs.text: The edge server runs chrony as the NTP server for both networks (with its own clock as a stratum-8 fallback when it has no internet access); each device runs chrony as a client with the edge server as its only source, polling every 4 to 16 s. Timestamps on different nodes are correlated through the NTP-synchronised wall clock captured at the start signal of every run; the preflight stage refuses a run when a device's offset exceeds ntp_offset_threshold_ms (1 ms by default). On the wired management network the offset is sub-millisecond; measure it with chronyc tracking (checklist).

docs.title: Power sensors (optional)
docs.text: An INA260 measures the current through its internal shunt. Insert it in the 5 V supply line of each device (the supply's 5 V to IN+, IN- to the board's 5 V input; a common ground), power the sensor from the board's 3.3 V pin and connect SDA and SCL to GPIO 2 and GPIO 3. Enable I2C on the device (raspi-config or dtparam=i2c_arm=on in /boot/firmware/config.txt); the default I2C address is 0x40. Install the optional packages of requirements/power.in on the device and set monitoring.power: true in the scenario. The sensor reports current in steps of 1.25 mA, bus voltage in steps of 1.25 mV and power in steps of 10 mW.

docs.title: Package mirror and reproducibility
docs.text: All Python and Debian packages are installed from a versioned local mirror on the edge server (mirror_dir, served by testbed-mirror.service): wheels per lock file for x86_64 and aarch64, Debian packages fetched once through a reference device, a bare clone of HeadSplit at the pinned commit, and MANIFEST.json with the SHA-256 of every file. python -m src.provisioning.mirror verify detects any change. Re-running the provisioning scripts later therefore installs an identical software stack. The random seeds of every stochastic library are set at the start of every experiment to the scenario's seed, which is stored in the run metadata.

docs.title: Provisioning in order
docs.text:
1. Edge server: config.yaml and nodes.json from the examples; export the passphrase; scripts/provision/provision_edge_server.sh --allow-upstream.
  2. scripts/provision/build_mirror.sh wheels (and headsplit).
  3. Per device: flash the 64-bit image, scripts/provision/prepare_image.sh <node id> <boot partition>, boot on the switch.
  4. Once: scripts/provision/build_mirror.sh apt <node id> and build_mirror.sh manifest.
  5. Per device: scripts/provision/provision_device.sh <node id> [--llm].

Every script accepts --dry-run and prints the commands it would run; every step is idempotent. The thesis quotes about 25 minutes per device and two hours for the whole testbed; the scripts append their elapsed time to results/provisioning/timing.log so the figures can be measured on your hardware.

docs.title: Model weights
docs.text: Weights are prepared once with a fixed seed (train_and_run_benchmark.sh train, or copied from a checkpoint for the LLMs) and distributed to the devices by provision_device.sh from bs_models_dir, with a SHA256SUMS file checked on arrival. No training happens on the devices.

docs.title: Checking the set-up
docs.text: Open http://<edge server management address>:<nnpm_port>/: every node should show a green marker within a few seconds. Run scripts/base_station/run_full_benchmarking.sh examples/scenarios/baseline.yaml and check results/latest/ for the three output files. The complete list of what to verify on the hardware, with expected values, is hardware_validation_checklist.md.
